About: A one-day HKSTP symposium at Hong Kong Science Park's INNO², pairing academic robotics talks with industry perspectives on robotics and applications.

The dominant thread is fusing foundation models (LLMs / VLMs) with robot perception, planning and manipulation — especially task-oriented grasping, human-robot collaboration & safety, and tactile / wearable sensing — alongside robust autonomy and smart transport for Hong Kong.

03 · Insights

The symposium, talk by talk

A · Foundation models for grasping & control
01

Generalizable Task-Oriented Grasping with Foundation Models

Hong Zhang · task-oriented grasping · FoundationGrasp
The problem
  • Task-Oriented Grasping (TOG) = decide which object to grasp and how; learning beats classical grasping but is data-hungry
  • Use foundation models (LLMs + VLMs) to transfer knowledge and generalize across novel objects, tasks and grippers
  • Goal: from an RGB image + a language instruction (object + task) + gripper geometry, output a 6-DoF grasp pose
GraspGPT / FoundationGrasp
  • Pipeline: data generation → multi-modal feature representation → task-oriented grasp evaluation → loss
  • Object/grasp encoder (PointNet++), semantic encoder (BERT), geometric encoder (CLIP), trained with binary cross-entropy
  • LLM prompts generate language descriptions; web image retrieval augments visual diversity
Results & limits
  • GraspCLIP reaches ~83% mAP but struggles on novel classes; FoundationGrasp adds commonsense reasoning
  • ~90% grasp success across nine manipulation tasks, but full-manipulation success ~67% (limited relative-pose modeling, no force feedback)
  • Ablations: geometric knowledge is key for novel instances, semantic knowledge for novel tasks
[1] H. Zhang, “Generalizable Task-Oriented Grasping with Foundation Models,” HKSTP Symposium on Innovative Robotics & Applications, 2024.
02

Robotics in the Artificial Intelligence Era

Ning Xi · LLM-driven robot control
From task planning to LLMs
  • Classical approach: build a task-plan sequence, then actions per task, executed by sensors + a control system
  • Now LLMs can control the robot directly, supplying the logical relationships and reasoning between actions
What an LLM must capture
  • Temporal relationships (e.g. past trajectory) and interactive spatial relationships (e.g. force to grasp a coffee cup)
  • Needs a new way to represent information, including unstructured constraints; control should be vision-based, not vector-based
The gap
  • LLM logical reasoning of motion (PaLM-style) vs robotic action: spatial sensing, world modeling, temporal/body acting, environment interaction
  • Framed as a Data-Driven vs Model-Driven challenge in AI
[2] N. Xi, “Robotics in the Artificial Intelligence Era,” HKSTP Symposium on Innovative Robotics & Applications, 2024.
03

Learning Dynamic Legged Loco-Manipulation

Koushil Sreenath · UC Berkeley
LLM as a feedback controller
  • Frame the LLM as a discrete-time nonlinear dynamic feedback controller with defined state, input and output
  • An LLM-interaction loop generates responses that close the control loop
Action generation
  • ‘Diffusion for Actions’ generates actions for dynamic legged loco-manipulation
[3] K. Sreenath, “Adventures in Learning Dynamic Legged Loco-Manipulation,” HKSTP Symposium on Innovative Robotics & Applications, 2024.
B · Human-robot collaboration & sensing
04

Collaboration & Interaction of Human-Robot and Robot-Robot

Masayoshi Tomizuka · UC Berkeley · Mechanical Systems Control Lab
Efficient, non-conservative co-robots
  • Robots raise efficiency, but automated robots tend to become conservative and slow the whole system
  • Challenge: design co-robot behavior so efficiency isn't sacrificed for safety
The SERoCS framework
  • Safe & Efficient Robot Collaboration System in three tasks: environment monitoring, task planning, safe control
  • Trade-off framed as Efficiency vs Safety under Computation vs Uncertainty
Controller & learning
  • A two-part controller with a safety-checker stage; uses an offline-learned human-motion prediction + nominal optimal control
  • RL for palletizing: pallet height-map + box size → feasibility map; task planning via RL with action masking
  • Methods: SERoCS, Conditional Behavior Prediction, Courteous Autonomous Cars
[4] M. Tomizuka, “Collaboration and Interaction of Human-Robot and Robot-Robot,” HKSTP Symposium on Innovative Robotics & Applications, 2024.
05

Logistics Application of Tactile Sensing with Smart Grippers

Hannah Stuart · UC Berkeley · Embodied Dexterity Group
Grasping without vision
  • Flexible logistics application of tactile sensing with smart grippers; one gripper alone may not suffice
  • Goal: find the optimum grasp position without an image sensor, using tactile feedback
The visual-tactile grasp loop
  • Grasp location is selected visually; grasp success is used as binary feedback
  • Grasp location is not modified after contact is made (ICRA 2015, Amazon Picking Challenge)
[5] H. Stuart, “Logistics Application of Tactile Sensing with Smart Grippers,” HKSTP Symposium on Innovative Robotics & Applications, 2024.
06

Amoeba-Inspired Self-Healing Electronic Slime as Wearable Motion Sensors

Wen Jung Li · wearable MEMS sensing
Amoeba-inspired self-healing sensor
  • A self-healing electronic ‘slime’ material for wearable motion sensing, inspired by amoeba
  • Monitors motion / behavior (demonstrated on a mouse) with a wearable MEMS sensor
Fabrication & use
  • Skin-conformal sensor fabricated via micro 3D printing
  • Targets human–robot interaction through wearable motion capture
[6] W. J. Li, “Amoeba-Inspired Self-Healing Electronic Slime as Wearable Motion Sensors for Human-Robot Interaction,” HKSTP Symposium, 2024.
C · Robust autonomy & smart transport
07

Enabling Autonomy with Robust Perception and Remote Intervention

Dan Wei Wang · robust perception & autonomy
Robust perception under adverse conditions
  • Current perception & navigation technologies are limited to normal conditions
  • ‘Adverse is various, adverse is challenging’: inclement weather causes appearance change, domain shift and urban haze
  • Perception and cognition algorithms are vulnerable to adverse events — motivating remote intervention as a fallback
[7] D. W. Wang, “Enabling Autonomy with Robust Perception and Remote Intervention,” HKSTP Symposium on Innovative Robotics & Applications, 2024.
08

Technological Development for Smart Transport in Hong Kong

Chun Hung Cheng · LSCM
System-design philosophy
  • Systems typically have many competing objectives (e.g. quiet, autonomous)
  • Don't build the system first and try to control it afterwards — co-design controls and mechanical design simultaneously
  • Treat control theory as a lens and a tool from the very start
[8] C. H. Cheng, “LSCM's Perspective on Technological Development for Smart Transport in Hong Kong,” HKSTP Symposium, 2024.
04 · Conclusions

Synthesis across the symposium

Trends

  • Foundation models are moving into the loop: LLMs / VLMs replace hand-built task-planning pipelines, supplying semantic, spatial, temporal and commonsense knowledge.
  • Task-oriented grasping is the benchmark problem — generalizing across novel objects, tasks and grippers via multi-modal fusion (BERT + CLIP + PointNet++).
  • Tactile and wearable sensing push perception beyond cameras (smart grippers, self-healing skin sensors).

Vision

  • Reframe the LLM itself as a dynamic feedback controller and the reasoning layer for motion — from planner to closed-loop element.
  • Universal, generalizable manipulation policies usable across many household robots and gripper types.
  • Robots that collaborate safely and efficiently with humans, without defaulting to conservative behavior.

Implications for us

  • Persistent gaps (efficiency-vs-safety; ~90% grasp vs ~67% full-manipulation success) show autonomy is bottlenecked by force feedback, relative-pose modeling and conservatism — not perception alone.
  • Robustness under adverse conditions and remote intervention are needed before deployment at scale.
  • Co-design control with mechanical design — treat control theory as a tool from the start, not an afterthought.
